The defendant can be convicted of murder under the doctrine of transferred intent, or alternatively under the felony-murder rule. He intentionally shot at the opposing player in order to injure him, which is an intentional, unlawful use of a firearm that would be at least aggravated battery or assault with a deadly weapon. In most jurisdictions that intent transfers to the unintended victim. Because the act showed extreme recklessness and disregard for human life, it supports a conviction for second-degree murder, which is probably the most serious charge available. First-degree murder is unlikely because there was no premeditated intent to kill.

CONFIDENCE: 66
